newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold shares finished up in quiet Thursday trade as some short-covering pushed gold share prices slightly higher ahead of U.S. Independence Day public holiday on Friday, dealers said.

They said bullion's hold between $331 and $332 an ounce level also helped the precious metal stocks off the ropes after the bullion's recent slide which saw the gold index fall through the 1,000 level on June 27, for the first time in four years.
"It looks like golds are up on a bit of short-covering by the looks of things," one Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) dealer said.

"(With) too few sellers, anybody looking to buy some gold stocks to cover short positions ahead of the U.S. long weekend are having to pay up...That's pretty much what is happening in the gold market," the dealer said.
The gold index was last up 20.5 points at 985.2, and dealers said a softer rand also provided support.
"The gold price is a little bit better and the rand is still slightly weak," one dealer said.

Among individual gold shares which benefitted were Vaal Reefs which added 500 cents to finish at 228.50 rand, Freegold which added 100 cents to 24.50 rand, Dries which climbed 65 cents to 31.15 rand and Eastvaal which added 37 cents to 485 cents.
While golds glistened through most of the day, industrial shares failed to budge onto positive territory as in the past four market days in which they have ended at new record closes.
Dealers said the market was likely to have started to consolidate following the recent gains and was seen holding slightly weaker ahead of the weekend on Friday.
They added that some profit-taking had also put the industrails under pressure on the day.
"I think the market has started a bit of consolidation after the recent bounce," Johan Marais, a director at stockbroking firm Societe Generale Frankel Pollak told Reuters.
The dealers said volumes were moderate with 695 million rand worth of shares exchanging hands around the close.
In the broader market decliners led advancers by 181 to 160, while 28 shares surged to new highs and 19 shares sank to new lows.
The industrial index finished down 2.7 points at 8,829.8, and the all-share index was down 13.5 points at 7,403.2.

But dealers said underlying sentiment remained positive with strong foreign interest and despite the industrial index finishing weaker, most industrial shares managed to end higher with SA Breweries gaining 50 cents to 140.00 rand.
Engineering to construction firm Murray & Roberts gained 24 cents to 922 cents on renewed interest after the stock sank to new year lows following the company's profit warning on Tuesday.
On the financials side, insurance group Liberty Life finished up 375 cents to 128.00 rand following a foreign sale by stockbroking house SBC Warburg of 200,000 shares worth around 25 million rand.
Dealers said the South African share futures market was also hit by some profit-taking.
The September industrial contract was last at 8,680/95 from 8,677 settlement, the gold contract was at 690/702 from 690 settlement and the all-share contract was at 6,810/20 from 6,835.
-- Ellis Mnyandu, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
